intended_object: A scheme morphism over Spec K, G_a^{gap-r superdiagonal} → U_r (the r-th stage of the unitriangular filtration, as a scheme). It sends coordinates (x_{ij}) to the matrix with those entries on the r-th superdiagonal and zeros on the higher superdiagonals. It is a set-theoretic/scheme section, not a group homomorphism, of the stage coordinate map U_r → G_a^m. This reading comes from the docstring, the module doc and the companion lemma `_comp`.
explanation: The definition chains three maps: the identification of the categorical product of additive group schemes with Spec of a polynomial ring, then Spec of `MvPolynomial.killCompl` (which sends the higher-gap variables to zero and keeps the gap-r variables), then the inverse of the identification of the stage scheme with Spec of a polynomial ring in the surviving entries. Its only role is to supply an explicit right inverse for the underlying scheme map of the stage coordinate morphism. That is what lemma `unitriangularStageCoordinateSectionOver_comp` records, and its docstring explicitly says no group-scheme splitting or published theorem is asserted. So this is an auxiliary construction used in a proof (a non-canonical splitting that depends on coordinates and is transported through library-specific isomorphisms), not a standard object from the literature. As a construction it does what it says: it works for any commutative ring K, and killing the complementary variables is the right formula for the section x ↦ I + Σ x_{ij} E_{i,i+r}. Mathlib has no counterpart, since unitriangular group schemes and their filtration are not in Mathlib.
